hypothesis.title: A restart pulls every still-held planned crash of another node into a learned post-restart window
hypothesis.description: Cascade crash placement anchored on the restart event. On a salted half of the placed runs (own salt over fault_timing::is_placed ids, probes exempt by inheritance; bit restartPulledCrash = 1<<4, the retired staleOrder row renamed), at every restart apply of node p at step s (core/scheduler.rs recover_crashed_node), every other node n with crash_pending > 0 whose placement target crash_hold_until[n] lies past s + S is re-targeted to s + ((old_target) mod (S + 1)). The offset reuses the old target's randomness, so no stream is drawn and treated and untreated twins keep every random stream in step; the pull only ever shortens a hold, so nothing can starve. S is learned per backup-budget scope exactly as fault_timing learns its median: a 256-cell histogram of the ghost lag - at every message entry whose origin restarted since sending (origin_incarnation != current incarnation, origin live) at a live destination other than the origin, lag = entry_step - origin's last restart step (new SendLedger field last_restart_step set in recover_crashed_node) - fed by stock-posture run-cap probes only, quantile 0.90 read at the winning cell's upper edge, 200-sample floor, doubling checkpoints, same decay and reset. Below the floor no pull happens (identity). The phase stage (crash_phase Early/Mid/Stock on anchored runs) is untouched: its slot stays Pending and draws at the first hold() call after the new target, so the pulled crash then waits up to WINDOW for the victim's fan-out as it does today; ghost-absorber retarget at apply is unchanged. S is stored on State at run start (path.rs, from fault_timing::lag_quantile(backup)) so the scheduler needs no path-local. Counters in util_stats.rs under crash_place.restart_pull: pulls, restarts_with_held_crash, steps_saved_sum, lag_p90 gauge per scope, scopes_engaged, and applied_within_window per cell (crashes applied within S steps of the most recent restart of another node). No config field.
hypothesis.rationale: Crashes are plan roots (judge note on crash-release-anchored-on-outstanding-client-work), so every placed crash draws its target uniformly over [0, U) with U the learned median completed length; two crashes' targets are independent, and the chance that the later one lands within tens of steps after the earlier node's restart - where that node's dead-incarnation records land at live peers and the peers react - is about S/U, a few percent. The oracle chain needs exactly that: label 5 is a crash of the node that just absorbed the first crash's ghost, landing with its reaction fan-out in flight, and labels 8 and 9 are that reaction's stranded records. The counters agree: depth 4 to 5 converts at 0.205 (174,086 -> 35,694 per chunk) even though depth 3 to 4 converts at 0.99, and the retarget releases find no absorber mark on two thirds of releases (victim_swap.no_absorber 321,307 of 479,257) because the target usually falls long after the marks were made and cleared. ghost_signal.fired_runs = 383,582 per chunk says a ghost lands on a node with a pending crash in 48 percent of runs; the pull moves the crash to that neighbourhood on purpose. The closed reaction-triggered arm (iteration 17) expired on 0.83 of armings because it armed at a uniform target and waited 96 steps; arming at the restart, whose ghost lag p90 is what S measures (recovery_window p50 6, p90 21 events for the first entry back at the restarted node; the lag to a live peer is of that order), is the correction. The pull never lengthens a run, so throughput cannot fall from the hold side.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Restart, dead-incarnation entry at a live peer, and a withheld planned crash are simulator event classes; no handler, message or role is named. The only constant, S, is learned from the protocol under test's own probes as the p90 of its ghost lag, so another protocol gets its own window and nobody sets a value. Correlated faults during another node's rejoin is the standard fault-injection stratum for recovery bugs (stale-ballot, stale-vote and stale-scout members of the panel are all reached by a crash that strands a reaction to stale traffic).

hypothesis.notes: Parent of the two nested cells below; each nested cell is read against this cell's pull-only half.
hypothesis.redTeam: The pull moves a late second crash into [s, s+S]. The ghost lag has median 6 in a window of about 20, so on roughly a third of pulled crashes the crash now lands BEFORE the ghost reaches the victim - the too-early shape that already loses 80 percent of runs at the depth 4->5 transition - and those runs are lost, not gained; the pull-only cell can read down on depth 5 and flat on depth 8, with the gain confined to the nested trigger cell. The candidate misreads victim_swap.no_absorber: ghost marks are cleared only by clear_ghost_mark at the absorber's own crash and the absorber ranking has no recency window, so the no-absorber mass is the too-early case, which the pull does not touch when the target already sits before the restart and can add to when it pulls a target into the window ahead of the ghost. Second, the segment the crash must strand is the victim's ghost-woken reaction, and the closed reaction arm measured such segments as broadcasts on only 8.4 percent of its releases; a crash landed on the reaction mostly strands one send, while depth 8 and 9 need two of that segment's sends to the restarted peer undelivered. Third, the pull fires only when a crash is pending with a target past s+S at the restart; with crash-to-restart intervals of a few steps and the exempt plan cell, the second crash is often unreleased or already targeted before s, so 150,000 pulls on about 355,000 treated runs is not assured. Fourth, on a three-node system a crash within tens of steps of a restart takes down the one peer the restarted node may still need; the nested reply-wait cell predicts exactly that as a depth-8 cost, and the pull-only cell carries it unmeasured.
hypothesis.scoreReason: A verified, well-sited mechanism: the second crash's timing relative to the first restart is unconditioned today (targets uniform over [t_ready, U) from independent draws), the learned window is the protocol's own ghost lag, stream parity is kept without a draw, the landing is counted by an observable the explorer reads at run end, and the internal contrast stays clean because the pull only shortens holds (composition changes, the budget does not; the control is not unbalanced upward on steps). Marked down for one false mechanism claim (no_absorber attributed to marks clearing), for the depth-5 direction risk its band did not admit, and for leaning on the nested trigger to fix the before-the-ghost half; the depth-8 lower edge is widened to 1.03 with depth>=5 reported and depth>=9 as the advance read. First of the new crash-placement family; the trigger cell is built with it in the same session on its own salt, the reply-wait cell later. It supersedes the queued crash-holds-for-restarted-peer-delivery-window as the restart-window mechanism: same aim, but a learned window rather than a 96-step hold on a predicate that is true on most post-restart steps, and no lengthening; the two share the crash_hold_until actuator and must not be built in one session.

nestedHypothesis.title: Inside the pull window, the crash is released by the first acted dead-incarnation entry at a live peer
nestedHypothesis.description: Nested cell inside the pull's treated half (own salt; bit ghostTriggeredCrash = 1<<28, the retired clientProgressRelease row renamed; set only together with 1<<4). On these runs the restart of p at step s does not draw a uniform offset: every pulled crash's target becomes s + S (the window's end) and a trigger is armed on p. At the delivery site in core/scheduler.rs, where `ghost` and `acted` are already computed, the first message entry after s at a live node v other than p from p's dead incarnation (r.origin_node == p, r.origin_incarnation != current) that changes v's state sets crash_hold_until[n] = current_step + 1 for every pulled crash n and disarms the trigger. The crash then enters the phase stage at the next step while v's reaction segment is its current segment, so Early's predicate (segment issued, nothing delivered) is true at once on runs whose phase read lands on v (the retarget's absorber ranking picks the node that just took an acted ghost). If no such entry occurs by s + S the crash proceeds at s + S as the pull-only cell would at its latest. Nothing is drawn; the trigger only moves a target earlier inside the window. Counters under crash_place.restart_pull.trigger: armed, fired, expired, and steps_from_restart_sum at firing.
nestedHypothesis.rationale: The uniform pull lands the crash before the ghost on roughly half its window and relies on the 96-step phase window to catch the reaction; the trigger lands it exactly one step after the reaction segment starts, when every send of that segment is undelivered and the absorber mark is one step old. ghost_signal.fired_runs = 383,582 per chunk (48 percent of runs) is a lower bound on how often the trigger has an occasion, since it counts only ghosts landing on nodes with a pending crash; crash_phase.early.expired is 54,734 of 402,367 armings and bucket_1 at apply 62,471 - both are the crash arriving off the reaction's step. The closed reaction arm's 0.83 expiry came from arming at a uniform target; here the trigger is armed at the restart and bounded by the learned lag p90, so most arms fire.
nestedHypothesis.generalityArgument: The trigger is the generic event class 'a record from a dead incarnation of the node that just restarted enters a live peer and changes its state'. It names no handler; the bound S is the parent's learned window. On any protocol the peer's reaction to stale traffic is the segment a crash must strand to leave a stale reply in flight.

nestedHypothesis.notes: Bit 1<<28 is a retired row with no mechanism on the merged tree (the plan-progress clock closed at iteration 78).
nestedHypothesis.redTeam: The trigger fires on an acted ghost at v and releases every pulled crash n, but the reaction segment is at v; the crash lands on v only on the retarget half (bit 1<<19) or when the plan victim happens to be v (one in two on three nodes), so about a third of the cell's crashes strand a segment on a node that did not react and the whole-cell band is diluted. Acted ghost entries are 18.6 percent of sender-restarted deliveries on the fresh cache, so fired/armed near 0.45 is optimistic; on a miss the crash lands at s+S, the window's END, later than the pull-only cell's uniform landing, draining more of the reaction - an under-firing trigger cell can read below the pull-only cell on depth 8. 'Changes v's state' is the state token compare, which counts any handler write, so the trigger can fire on an acted-but-inert ghost (a bookkeeping write with no send) and strand nothing. The closed reaction arm's 8.4 percent broadcast share says the ghost-woken segment is usually a single send even when the crash lands on it exactly.
nestedHypothesis.scoreReason: The corrective for the parent's main weakness (a crash pulled ahead of the ghost): the trigger is generic (a dead-incarnation record from the node that just restarted acts at a live peer), the sites exist (ghost and acted are computed at the delivery site), the landing is counted, nothing is drawn, and it reads against the pull-only half on the internal rung. Built WITH the parent in the same session as its nested cell, because without it the pull-only cell carries the before-the-ghost loss unanswered. Marked down for the dilution across non-retarget runs and the optimistic firing share; the bands and the firing share are rewritten and a retarget-stratum read added. Internal contrast: composition only; the trigger moves a target earlier inside the window, so the control is not unbalanced on steps.

reviewSummary: Fourteen candidates judged blind against the merged tree (spur 98e9a93), the fresh merged-tree cache 17a424fcac21, the pool and the oracle DAG. The proposer's reading of the path checks out against traceanalyzer dagorder's root-anchored prefix: depth 4 deliver_svc_1_to_2, 5 crash_2, 6 recover_2, 7 deliver_rec_2_to_1, 8 deliver_svc_2_to_1, 9 deliver_dvc_2_to_1, 10 w2, no crash label after depth 5; the cited conversions (4->5 0.205, 3->4 0.99, 8->9 0.16) match the cache. The three new crash-placement candidates are one family: the restart pull stands first (net 6) with its trigger cell built with it in the same session on its own salt (net 5) and the reply-wait cell built later, after the pull has read (net 4). The pull supersedes the queued crash-holds-for-restarted-peer-delivery-window as the restart-window mechanism (same aim; learned window instead of a 96-step hold on a predicate that ghost sends satisfy; shortens instead of lengthens); the queued entry is kept at net 3 as the fallback and must not share a session with the pull. The defer-coin exemption (net 5) is independent and cheapest. One checkable claim found false: the pull's attribution of victim_swap.no_absorber to ghost marks having been 'made and cleared' - marks are cleared only by clear_ghost_mark at the absorber's own crash and the ranking has no recency window, so the no-absorber mass is the too-early case, which the pull can worsen on the share of the window ahead of the ghost; the pull's depth-8 band is widened at the bottom, depth>=5 is reported and depth>=9 made the advance read. Bit contest resolved: the replay-arm pair keeps 1<<22/1<<23; the defer-coin exemption takes 1<<16 and the reply-wait cell 1<<25, freed by rejecting run-cap-headroom-one-dose (premise removed by the stall-cap merge) and stall-release-of-withheld-faults (superseded by the repeat). Bit 1<<4 (staleOrder) is confirmed retired, absent from NON_DECLARABLE_BITS and unread in spur-core. Internal contrasts: the pull, trigger and coin exemption only shorten holds, so their per-run controls are clean on composition; the reply-wait cell and the queued crash-holds add suspended holds up to 96 steps and carry steps-per-run guards. Stale figures corrected on the carried entries (parents admitted, stall stops, replay fidelity, run-cap figures, per-step counter totals, timer fires per run); the repeat release's depth-10 band is lowered to [1.06, 1.35] on the fresh cache's event counts.

otherCandidates.scoreReason: Every claim checked out: the two masks are OR'd (scheduler.rs:822), the coin is drawn per step for every pending crash while in_flight != 1 at partial_fanout_crash_bias 0.5 and keeps rolling after a phase release, on_condition is already tracked, and the Early apply-time buckets and release counts match the fresh cache exactly. The fix is a clean composition statement about the explorer (two randomizers on one crash pulling opposite ways) with parity kept by drawing and discarding, a bucket observable the explorer reads at run end, and an internal contrast with no shared state. Marked down because the expected magnitude is small and the 3plus stratum is not the segment's own count. Independent of the pull family; runs in the same session on its own salt, or alone. Internal contrast: it removes withheld steps, so the control is not unbalanced upward on steps.
otherCandidates.redTeam: The coin's expected extra withholding after a condition release is one step (geometric at one half), and the victim's own sends drain at well under one per step on a three-node queue, so the erosion is a fraction of a send per crash; the bucket shift may be a few points, not 0.53 to 0.60, and the 1.12x observable floor is at risk. The apply-time buckets count all of the victim's undelivered sends, not the segment's: Early releases on three nodes are one- or two-send segments, and the 3plus mass comes largely from older undelivered sends the coin does not touch. The exemption also removes the coin's attractor toward exactly one in flight, which the merged census once showed as the stratum that grew; that trade is untested. The depth effect runs only through the 7->8 and 8->9 conversions on 0.22 of runs, where the resolvable internal effect is about 5 percent, so the band's lower edge sits under the resolution floor.
